name: Dyed black (pond black)
process: A water-soluble black dye is dissolved in the pond, a measured dose per volume, until the water is so absorbing that nothing below the surface can be seen: the pond becomes a black mirror. The dye blocks the light submerged algae need, so the water stays clear of green; plants whose leaves and flowers float on or stand above the surface (water lilies) are not affected. The dose fades and is topped up every few months.

powder.derivation: 200 g sachet 'treats 6,000 litres'; the 50 g sachet treats 1,500 L and the 1 kg pack 30,000 L, the same ratio
powder.source: Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/
powder.conditions: Dyofix Pond Black powder, cold-water-soluble sachets

liquid.derivation: 300 g bottle 'will treat up to 1000 litres of pond water'
liquid.source: Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/
liquid.conditions: Dyofix Pond Black liquid (a pre-dissolved concentrate)

endPoint.text: 'Pond Black has fully mixed in when you cannot see below the surface of the water. Don't add any more at this stage.'
endPoint.source: Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/

duration.source: Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/
duration.note: 'One application can last up to three months'

effect.text: The dye blocks light, 'allowing no light to penetrate below the surface, hence the black appearance'; it 'enhances your pond's reflective qualities' and makes it 'impossible to see the fish'.
effect.source: Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/

surfaceUnchanged.text: A dissolved dye changes the water's absorption, not its refractive index at the surface: the surface still reflects about 2 % face-on and a mirror's share at grazing (water.optics.fresnelUnpolarised). Black water looks like a mirror because nothing comes back from below to veil the reflection.
surfaceUnchanged.derivation: Fresnel reflectance of water (n from Daimon and Masumura) with the dye's stated effect of blocking all light below the surface
surfaceUnchanged.source: M. Daimon, A. Masumura (2007) 'Measurement of the refractive index of distilled water from the near-infrared region to the ultraviolet region', Applied Optics 46(18):3811-3820, https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.46.003811 ; Sellmeier coefficients for 20.0 degC as tabulated at https://refractiveindex.info/?shelf=main&book=H2O&page=Daimon-20.0C ; Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/
surfaceUnchanged.note: No measurement of dyed water's refractive index was found; a dilute dye is assumed not to change it.

plants.text: Plants that have leaves and flowers above the water are not affected; fish are safe but cannot be seen.
plants.source: Dyofix (Town End (Leeds) plc), 'Black pond dye: Pond Black', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.dyofix.co.uk/black-pond-dye/

composition.text: The dye's chemical identity and share are withheld as a trade secret in the one safety data sheet read; the mixture is not classified as hazardous.
composition.source: Lawn and Garden Products Inc., 'Monterey Black Pond Dye' Safety Data Sheet, product code 50020, issue 06-04-2015, sections 2 and 3, https://www.montereylawngarden.com/product/monterey-black-pond-dye/

photograph: Nothing below the surface: lily stems and the basin's lining vanish a finger's depth down.
The surface holds a crisp reflection of the velarium and the panels, broken only where the lily pads float.
At the edge, the water line on the stone is not bordered by a visible bed: black meets the coping directly.

unverified.reason: No absorption spectrum of a pond black dye at its dose was found. The manufacturer's end point (bed invisible) through the Salon pond's depth of about 0.32 m (the old build: water surface at h 0.38 m, bed at 0.06 m, windows/Source/MuseeVision/Salon/SalonPond.cpp) implies a two-way transmittance well under 1 %, i.e. an absorption above about 7 /m across the visible, if 1 % is taken as the visibility limit; that limit is an assumption.
Black food and acid dyes (for example C.I. Food Black 2) are candidates, but no pond-dye maker's composition was confirmed.
